title: Same tasks, different order
hook: Three short tasks, two kinds. Does the order change how long they take?

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that each switch has a setup cost, so grouping similar tasks cuts the number of switches and the time they use

misconception: Switching between kinds of task costs nothing, so their order doesn't matter.
objective: Compare setup overhead under an explicit switching cost.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Three short tasks, two kinds. Does the order change how long they take? Tasks A, B, A take 5 minutes each, and every change between A and B costs 2 minutes. Group the two A tasks: how many minutes does that save? Options: 2 minutes / 0: same three tasks / 4 minutes. Correct option: 2 minutes. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md. | Reset to unverified 2026-10-16 by demo-builder (batch B4, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/content-patch-2026-10-16-r2.md section 1): hook, question, options, answer replaced (row "batch-by-setup"). Not checked by the builder. | FC pass 61 (fact-checker, SO-10-2 Life Hacks set A, 2026-10-16; shared review server 5b2fee7, R3a pass; walkthrough on :3591 read first, cut at the appendix; numbers re-run in node from the engine on main 2d6b4d5): DISPUTED. Text matches studyCatalog (hook, question, options, answer 0). The key '2 minutes' is the finish-time saving (queueResult time 19 alternating vs 17 grouped), but the stage never shows a finish time: it measures 'Total waiting: each job's start time, added up' and shows 21 min (A1→B1→A2) against 17 min (A1→A2→B1), a 4-minute drop. 'Swap first' shows 19. So the distractor '4 minutes' is what the stage itself reports, and a learner who reads the stage is marked wrong. Fix (cm-lifehacks for the line, demo-builder implements): either ask for the stage's own metric ('Group the two A tasks: how much does total waiting drop?' with 4 minutes keyed and 2 minutes as the one-switch slip), or keep the 2-minute key and add the finish time ('all done at minute 19 / 17') to the stage and the question. Re-check after the change. Record: company/reviews/lifehacks-200/2026-10-16-fact-check-pass61.md.
